long-covid.title: SARS-CoV-2 seeds IAPP aggregation and β-cell failure.
long-covid.authors: Song, Zhiqi, Xu, Yanfeng, Zhao, Wenjie, Zhang, Ling et al.
long-covid.excerpt: The global diabetes incidence has surged post-COVID-19, yet how SARS-CoV-2 drives long-term beta cell (β-cell) failure remains incompletely elucidated. We identified a mechanism whereby SARS-CoV-2 structural proteins directly hijack islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) to induce pathogenic amyloid deposition, disrupting insulin granule maturation, trafficking, and secretion in an age-susceptible islet microenvironment.

long-covid.title: Trends in long COVID and post-viral fatigue in children in primary care in England.
long-covid.authors: Raveendran, Vishnuga, Thorne, Claire, Jackson, Charlotte, D'Souza, Rashmi et al.
long-covid.excerpt: Post-viral sequelae following the COVID-19 pandemic attention to post-viral fatigue and long COVID, but the impact on children and young people's (CYP) primary care use is unknown. To examine temporal, seasonal, and sociodemographic patterns in primary care consultations for long COVID and PVFS in We conducted a retrospective, population-based dynamic cohort study using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum data...

long-covid.title: Supporting the psychosocial well-being of patients with Long COVID: patient-informed strategies from a qualitative study.
long-covid.authors: Martinez, Bryce D, Shaw, Jonathan G, Asch, Steven M, Bragdon, Cassandra L et al.
long-covid.excerpt: Long COVID, an illness characterized by long-lasting symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection, exacts a substantial toll on psychosocial well-being and overall health. Persistent physiological symptoms and associated experiences can negatively impact employment, daily functioning, identity, and social relationships.

long-covid.title: Persistent Immune Thrombocytopenia as a Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19: A Case Report.
long-covid.authors: Riazullah, Wazir, Hakim Ullah, Mujeeb, Aafeen, Ahmad, Hamid et al.
long-covid.excerpt: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is a recognized hematologic complication associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), but its persistence years after acute infection remains uncommon. We present a case of a 52-year-old male who was diagnosed with COVID-19 in June 2020.

long-covid.title: Multiomic and Spatial Profiling of Colorectal Tissue Reveals Viral Persistence and Immune Dysregulation in Long COVID.
long-covid.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
long-covid.authors: LaFranchi, Brian, Maison, David P, Vinden, Joanna, Rodriguez, Antonio E et al.
long-covid.excerpt: Long COVID (LC) - a chronic condition characterized by persistent, debilitating symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection - has emerged as a major public health challenge. Although many interrelated mechanisms have been proposed as drivers of LC, the root causes have yet to be identified, posing significant challenges for therapeutic development.

long-covid.title: Microtesla magnetic therapy for cognitive impairment in long COVID: a randomized pilot study.
long-covid.authors: Canori, Alexandra, Watson, Eric, Patel, Devanshi, Fiorentino, Arianna et al.
long-covid.excerpt: Cognitive impairment is common in post-acute sequelae of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection (long COVID) and substantially affects function and quality of life. Evidence suggests that sustained neuroinflammation, cerebrovascular dysfunction and mitochondrial impairment contribute to cognitive symptoms.

long-covid.title: Incidence and Determinants of Post-Coronavirus Disease Syndrome by Disease Severity: An Ambispective Cohort Study from a Tertiary Care Hospital in Puducherry.
long-covid.journal: Indian journal of community medicine : official publication of Indian Association of Preventive & Social Medicine
long-covid.authors: Renjana, S R, Duraiswamy, Mahadevan, Jayaseelan, Venkatachalam, Radjasegarane, Arulprasad et al.
long-covid.excerpt: Post-coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) condition, or long COVID, persists beyond the acute phase, impacting quality of life. This study estimated the incidence and determinants of post-COVID syndrome (PCS) in Puducherry, India.

long-covid.title: Health Care Expenditures and Cost-Sharing Before and After Long COVID: Three-Year Evidence From a Statewide Multi-Payer Cohort.
long-covid.journal: Medical care research and review : MCRR
long-covid.authors: DeVoss, Rick, Carlton, Elizabeth J, Perraillon, Marcelo C
long-covid.excerpt: The objective of this study was to quantify expenditures for long COVID (LC) before/after diagnosis and compare 3-year trajectories with similar patients without LC in claims. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using Colorado All Payer Claims Database multi-payer claims (October 1, 2020-August 1, 2024).

long-covid.title: Exercise effectiveness on fatigue in Long-COVID: systematic review and meta-analysis.
long-covid.journal: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine
long-covid.authors: Chen, Yi-Chun, Yang, Hui-Ting, Wu, Chu-Fang, Kuo, Chia-Chi
long-covid.excerpt: Patients with Long COVID commonly experience fatigue-related distress, often leading to low energy, reduced activity endurance, and exertional dyspnea, all of which negatively impact quality of life. Although studies have increasingly explored the effects of exercise on Long COVID-related fatigue, a comprehensive synthesis of the evidence is lacking.

long-covid.title: Depleted before the dose: the mitochondrial vulnerability threshold hypothesis for fluoroquinolone-associated multisystem toxicity.
long-covid.authors: Sewell, Patrick E, Jensen, Christopher J
long-covid.excerpt: Fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics have an established capacity for mitochondrial injury, yet only a subset of exposed patients develop severe or persistent toxicity. We propose the Mitochondrial Vulnerability Threshold (MVT) hypothesis: that whether a standard therapeutic FQ dose produces clinically significant toxicity may depend substantially on the patient's pre-existing mitochondrial reserve capacity rather than...

long-covid.title: Could persistent extravascular fibrin deposition link microvascular and interstitial pathology in long COVID?
long-covid.excerpt: Long COVID is associated with persistent endothelial dysfunction, microvascular impairment, coagulation abnormalities, impaired fibrinolysis, and tissue hypoxia. Although these intravascular abnormalities are increasingly documented, less attention has been paid to whether vascular injury may also generate persistent pathology in the extravascular interstitial compartment.

long-covid.title: Bridging the gap in Long COVID care: identifying core competencies for primary care curriculum development and evaluation.
long-covid.authors: Geyer, Rachel E, O'Loughlin, Kristen M, Theobald, Cassie, Rivera, Donovan et al.
long-covid.excerpt: There is an unmet need for Long COVID care within our healthcare system. Primary care clinicians (PCPs) face challenges in providing effective care due to limited relevant Long COVID training and lack of standardized clinical resources.

long-covid.title: A cognitive architecture for Long COVID: the interplay of brain fog, fatigue, attention and memory.
long-covid.authors: Higgins, Darragh, Zhao, Sijia, Husain, Masud, Denno, Peter et al.
long-covid.excerpt: The cognitive mechanisms underlying post-acute COVID-19 sequelae ('Long COVID') remain poorly defined. While deficits in memory and executive function are well-documented, it is unclear whether these arise from primary neural dysfunction or are secondary consequences of fatigue-related factors.

gulf-war-illness.title: Deposition, Retention, and Clearance of Depleted Uranium and Tungsten Following Inhalation Exposure: Biokinetic Analysis and Implications for Long-term Health Effects.
gulf-war-illness.authors: Keifer, Lydia J, Mate-Kole, Emmanuel Matey, Dewji, Shaheen Azim
gulf-war-illness.excerpt: This study evaluates respiratory deposition and subsequent biokinetic behavior of DU and W aerosols using computational modeling informed by reported military exposure conditions. Particle deposition fractions in the respiratory tract were calculated using REDCALdep, which implements the ICRP Publication 66 respiratory tract deposition model with relevant updates from ICRP Publication 130.

pots.title: The link between inflammation and autonomic dysfunction in alpha-synucleinopathies - narrative review.
pots.authors: Kutyłowski, Karol, Alster, Piotr, Madetko-Alster, Natalia
pots.excerpt: Alpha-synucleinopathies are a group of disorders characterized by the accumulation of the pathological form of alpha-synuclein. This group comprises Parkinson's disease, Parkinson's disease dementia, multiple system atrophy, dementia with Lewy bodies, pure autonomic failure, and idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder.

pots.title: Targeting Brain-Body Processes in Postural Tachycardia Syndrome: A Pilot Trial of POts Reprocessing Therapy.
pots.authors: Crouch, Taylor B, Chase, Spencer, Redman, Tammy, Wells, Mary et al.
pots.excerpt: Purpose Postural tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is a chronic autonomic disorder characterized by orthostatic intolerance and frequently accompanied by a broad constellation of debilitating symptoms. Emerging evidence suggests that dysregulation within central-autonomic regulatory networks may contribute to symptom persistence.

mcas.title: [Beyond the placebo effect: exploring the mast cell-dependent analgesic effect of shallow needling control].
mcas.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
mcas.authors: Luo, Zhengrong, Zhang, Youwen, Ge, Xiaolei, Tian, Xinyi et al.
mcas.excerpt: Based on the distribution characteristics of mast cells and existing mechanistic evidence, the study explores the potential biological effects of shallow needling control (sham-acupuncture). Regarding cellular distribution, mast cells exhibit a physiological characteristic of dense distribution in both the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, predominantly in the distal regions, and show a higher density in acupoint...

mcas.title: Type I autoimmunity in chronic spontaneous urticaria: Evidence, limits, and endotype overlap.
mcas.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
mcas.authors: Konstantinou, George N, Grattan, Clive E H
mcas.excerpt: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a mast cell-driven disorder with basophil involvement and several possible upstream mechanisms. Type IIb autoimmune CSU, mediated by functional IgG autoantibodies against FcεRIα or IgE, is the best-validated endotype.

mcas.title: Systemic Allergic Reactions to mRNA COVID-19 Vaccines: A Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.
mcas.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
mcas.authors: Wheatley, Lisa M, Baker, James R, Adkinson, N Franklin, Gruchalla, Rebecca et al.
mcas.excerpt: COVID-19 mRNA vaccines were associated in early reports with more allergic reactions than most vaccines, especially in people with allergic histories. To estimate the proportions of systemic allergic reactions to mRNA COVID-19 vaccines in people reporting prior severe allergic reactions to various allergens, and/or mast cell disorders (PSAR/MCD Group) and determine if proportions are higher than in non-PSAR/non-MCD...

mcas.title: Estradiol-associated extracellular signaling in the human breast
mcas.authors: Abrahamsson, Annelie, Wang, Xingyue, Zhong, Wen, Dabrosin, Charlotta
mcas.excerpt: Sex steroid exposure is a major risk factor for breast cancer initiation and progression through incompletely understood mechanisms. Novel therapeutics for prevention and treatment of estrogen-dependent breast cancer are needed.

mcas.title: Luteolin alleviates neurogenic inflammation in OVA-induced combined allergic rhinitis and asthma syndrome mice through TRPV1/ERK-related signaling.
mcas.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
mcas.authors: Li, Jing, Mirodilova, Firuza, Lei, Lei
mcas.excerpt: Combined Allergic Rhinitis and Asthma Syndrome (CARAS), a common chronic allergic respiratory disease, involves dysregulated neuro-immune interactions and neurogenic inflammation. Luteolin (LUT) has significant anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities.

mcas.title: LL-37-MRGPRX2-Mast Cell Signaling in Rosacea: Current Evidence and Directions for Human Studies.
mcas.excerpt: This critical narrative review examines evidence relevant to LL-37-Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2)-mast-cell signaling in rosacea and considers the relevance of these findings to future human studies. Literature was identified through PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection searches, supplemented by examination of reference lists from relevant original studies and recent reviews.

mcas.title: Inducible Laryngeal Obstruction in Hypermobile Patients.
mcas.authors: Menton, Stacey M, Fairweather, DeLisa, Wilson, Frances C, Zangerle, Derek J et al.
mcas.excerpt: To determine whether patients with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS) or hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD) and inducible laryngeal obstruction (ILO) have more voice, cough, swallowing, GI issues, and MC activation than patients without ILO. This retrospective study of 2162 patients meeting 2017 diagnostic criteria for hEDS (n = 507) or HSD (n = 1655) who were seen at the EDS Clinic in Mayo Clinic Florida...

mcas.title: Mast cell activation syndrome: Global perspectives from a World Allergy Organization survey on knowledge, diagnosis, and access to care.
mcas.authors: Giavina-Bianchi, Pedro, Giavina-Bianchi, Mara, Morais-Almeida, Mário, Álvarez-Twose, Iván et al.
mcas.excerpt: Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) has emerged as a highly debated and increasingly recognized condition in allergy and clinical immunology. Despite established AIM/ECNM consensus criteria, major uncertainties persist regarding its diagnosis, implementation in real-world practice, and equitable access to diagnostic resources worldwide.

mcas.title: Food-Associated Kounis Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum and Diagnostic Considerations from a Case Report and Systematic Qualitative Synthesis of Published Cases.
mcas.authors: Sanchez-Fernandez, Sergio, Lasarte, Gabriel Gastaminza, Garófalo, Carmen D'Amelio, Paredes-Gutierrez et al.
mcas.excerpt: Kounis syndrome (KS) is a hypersensitivity-associated acute coronary syndrome. Food-associated KS remains poorly characterized, and its clinical presentation may be mimicked by non-immune food-related toxic reactions.

mcas.title: The dual and context-dependent role of mast cells in cutaneous wound healing and scar formation.
mcas.excerpt: Successful tissue repair depends on the precise orchestration of phase-specific cellular responses alongside sustained activity of multifunctional immune regulators. Mast cells, which have primarily been long regarded as effector cells of allergic reactions, have emerged as pivotal modulators of wound repair.

mcas.title: Mechanistic insight into eosinophilic enteritis and related disorders.
mcas.authors: Syverson, Erin P, Venkatesh, Rajitha D, Bailey, Dominique D
mcas.excerpt: Eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases (EGIDs) affecting the gastrointestinal tract outside of the esophagus are categorized as non-EoE EGIDs, and knowledge regarding their natural history and pathophysiology is rapidly advancing. This review synthesizes evolving mechanistic insights in non-EoE EGID immunopathogenesis, emerging paradigms of disease development, and how these insights influence potential therapeutic...

mcas.title: Imperatorin exerts anti-colorectal cancer effects by targeting NOX2 to inhibit mast cell degranulation.
mcas.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
mcas.authors: Shi, Xianpeng, Zhang, Peng, Cui, Xia, Hou, Yajing et al.
mcas.excerpt: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major global malignancy with a poor prognosis in advanced stages. Aberrant mast cell activation within the tumor microenvironment (TME) drives CRC progression; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying the tumor-promoting role of mast cells in the hypoxic TME remain unclear, and effective therapies targeting these cells are lacking.

mcas.title: Tryptase Locus Variation Contributes to Normal-Range Basal Serum Tryptase Variability and Is Associated With Anaphylaxis.
mcas.journal: Clinical and experimental allergy : journal of the British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
mcas.authors: Svetina, Manca, Lyons, Jonathan J, Kopač, Peter, Šelb, Julij et al.
mcas.excerpt: Increased basal serum tryptase level (BST) is associated with anaphylaxis. In the absence of clonal mast cell disease and hereditary α-tryptasemia (HαT), the contribution of the tryptase locus variation to BST and anaphylaxis remains undefined.

mcas.title: Mast cell degranulation damages glymphatic system via PKC/p38MAPK/AQP4 to exacerbate hydrocephalus post intraventricular hemorrhage.
mcas.authors: Yang, Yijian, Ouyang, Qian, Wang, Junqiang, Wang, Kaiyue et al.
mcas.excerpt: Hydrocephalus following intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) remains a serious neurological condition with limited treatment options beyond invasive surgical interventions, underscoring the urgent need to elucidate its underlying mechanisms. Emerging evidence implicates impaired glymphatic system function in the pathogenesis of hydrocephalus, particularly through dysregulation of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) expression in...

mcas.title: Insulin Enhances Nitroglycerin-Induced Hyperalgesia Through Insulin-Responsive Receptor Signalling Involving the Trigeminovascular System and Meningeal Mast Cells.
mcas.authors: Torun, Ibrahim Ethem, Celik, Humeyra, Kilinc, Erkan, Kurtoglu, Muhammet Guzel
mcas.excerpt: Migraine headache prevalence is lower in patients with diabetes, but the underlying mechanisms remains unclear. This study explored the influences of hyperglycemia, insulin and insulin receptor (IR)/insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF-1R)-related signalling on migraine-related mechanisms in in vivo and ex vivo rat models.

mcas.title: From nasal cytology to cellular endotyping: mast cell-eosinophil interactions and overlapping inflammation in allergic rhinitis.
mcas.excerpt: Allergic rhinitis is traditionally defined by allergen sensitization and type 2 inflammation, yet increasing evidence indicates that this framework does not fully capture the biological heterogeneity of the nasal mucosa. The local inflammatory landscape reflects a dynamic interaction among epithelial cells, innate and adaptive lymphoid populations, mast cells, eosinophils, stromal elements, and vascular components...

other-post-viral.title: Metabolic basis of post-infectious sequelae after Ebola virus disease.
other-post-viral.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
other-post-viral.authors: Sanford, Anna C, Bond, Nell G, Ficenec, Samuel, Osterman, Charlotte et al.
other-post-viral.excerpt: Ebola virus disease (EVD) survivors often present with clinical sequelae after acute disease resolution, called post-Ebola syndrome (PES). Why some survivors develop these sequelae and others do not is poorly defined.
